definition: The share of predictions that lie within ±10 % of the observed values.
comment: Values close to 1 indicate accurate predictions.

definition: The proportion of correct predictions among all predictions.
comment: It is used for classification models.

definition: The coefficient of determination corrected for the number of predictors.
comment: It penalises models with more parameters.

definition: A model selection criterion equal to twice the number of parameters minus twice the maximised log-likelihood.
comment: Lower values indicate a better trade-off between fit and complexity.

definition: A goodness-of-fit statistic that weights the squared differences between empirical and fitted distribution functions, giving more weight to the tails.
comment: It is more sensitive to the tails than the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic.

definition: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of a classifier.
comment: It ranges from 0.5 (random) to 1 (perfect).

definition: The ratio of the computation time of a data assimilation run to that of a reference run.
comment: It measures the computational cost of assimilation.

definition: The mean of the percentage deviations between predicted and reference values.
comment: Positive and negative deviations may cancel out unless absolute values are used.

definition: A model selection criterion equal to the number of parameters times the logarithm of the sample size minus twice the maximised log-likelihood.
comment: It penalises complexity more than the AIC for large samples.

definition: The systematic difference between predicted and observed values.
comment: It is usually computed as the mean difference or as a ratio of means.

definition: The ratio of the mean of predicted values to the mean of observed values.
comment: A value of 1 indicates no bias.

definition: The sum over classes of the squared differences between observed and expected frequencies divided by the expected frequencies.
comment: It is used to test the fit of distributions to binned wind-speed data.

definition: The proportion of the variance of the observed values that is explained by the predictions.
comment: It ranges from minus infinity to 1 for out-of-sample predictions and from 0 to 1 for least-squares fits.

definition: The ratio of the standard deviation to the mean of a series.
comment: It measures relative dispersion and is often given in percent.

evaluationMetricName: Coefficient of variation of the RMSE
definition: The root mean square error divided by the mean of the observed values.
comment: It is equivalent to the relative RMSE.

definition: The time needed to run or train a model.
comment: It is used to compare the computational cost of methods.

definition: The ratio of the consistency index of a pairwise comparison matrix to the random index.
comment: It is used in the analytic hierarchy process; values below 0.1 are acceptable.

definition: The Akaike information criterion with a correction for small samples.
comment: It converges to the AIC for large samples.

definition: A measure of the strength and direction of the linear relationship between predicted and observed values.
comment: It ranges from -1 to 1.

definition: A goodness-of-fit statistic equal to the integrated squared difference between empirical and fitted distribution functions.
comment: It is used to compare the fit of probability distributions.

definition: A measure of the internal consistency of a set of survey items.
comment: Values above about 0.7 are usually considered acceptable.

definition: The difference between an estimated value and the corresponding reference value.
comment: Studies apply it to a quantity such as power, irradiation or temperature; the quantity is given by the result, not by the metric name.

definition: The absolute difference between the expected and the observed numbers of exceedances of a threshold.
comment: It evaluates how well a distribution reproduces extremes.

definition: The relative improvement of a forecast over a reference forecast such as persistence.
comment: Positive values indicate that the forecast beats the reference.

definition: A composite indicator that combines several scaled error and goodness-of-fit metrics to rank models.
comment: It is used in the solar radiation literature to rank empirical models.

definition: The share of pairwise judgements that are inconsistent.
comment: It is used to check expert judgements in multi-criteria methods.

definition: A standardised measure of the degree of model prediction error, from 0 (no agreement) to 1 (perfect agreement).
comment: It was proposed by Willmott in 1981.

definition: A symmetric measure of the difference between two probability distributions, based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence to their mean.
comment: It is bounded between 0 and 1 (base-2 logarithm) and equals 0 for identical distributions.

definition: A skill score combining correlation, variability ratio and bias ratio between simulated and observed values.
comment: It ranges from minus infinity to 1 and is used for hydrological models.

definition: The probability of observing a Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic at least as large as the one obtained if the fitted distribution is correct.
comment: A small p-value leads to rejecting the fitted distribution.

definition: The maximum absolute difference between the empirical and the fitted cumulative distribution functions.
comment: It is used to test and compare the fit of probability distributions to wind-speed data.

definition: The natural logarithm of the likelihood of the data under the fitted model.
comment: Higher values indicate a better fit for the same data.

definition: The largest absolute percentage difference between predicted and observed values.
comment: It reports the worst case rather than the average error.

definition: The largest absolute difference between two values divided by the reference value.
comment: It reports the worst case rather than the average deviation.

definition: The mean of the absolute differences between predicted and observed values.
comment: In the solar radiation literature it is used as a synonym of the mean absolute error.

definition: The mean of the absolute differences between values and their mean or between predicted and observed values.
comment: Its exact definition depends on the study.

definition: The mean of the absolute differences between predicted and observed values.
comment: It is expressed in the unit of the variable and is less sensitive to outliers than the RMSE.

definition: The mean of the absolute differences between predicted and observed values, relative to the observed values, in percent.
comment: It is scale independent but undefined when observed values are zero.

definition: The mean difference between two series.
comment: It is used when neither series is taken as the truth.

definition: The mean of the differences between predicted and observed values.
comment: A positive value indicates overestimation and a negative value underestimation.

definition: The mean of the importance scores given by respondents or experts to an item.
comment: It is used to rank barriers or drivers in surveys.

definition: The mean of the differences between predicted and observed values, relative to the observed values, in percent.
comment: Positive and negative errors cancel out, so it measures bias.

definition: The mean of the squared differences between predicted and observed values.
comment: It is the square of the RMSE.

definition: The time an algorithm needs to reach its operating point or solution.
comment: For maximum power point tracking it is the time to reach the maximum power point.

definition: A pseudo coefficient of determination for logistic regression, rescaled to reach 1.
comment: It is used for survey and adoption models with binary outcomes.

definition: One minus the ratio of the error variance of the simulated values to the variance of the observed values.
comment: It ranges from minus infinity to 1; it is the standard skill score of hydrological models.

definition: The negative of the natural logarithm of the maximum value of the likelihood function.
comment: Lower values indicate a better fit for the same data.

definition: The mean absolute error divided by a normalising quantity such as the mean of the observed values.
comment: The normalising quantity varies between studies.

definition: The root mean square error divided by a normalising quantity such as the mean or the range of the observed values.
comment: The normalising quantity varies between studies.

definition: The ratio of the odds of an outcome in one group to the odds in another group.
comment: In logistic regression it measures the effect of a factor on the outcome.

definition: The fraction of observations that fall within the 95 % prediction uncertainty band of a calibrated model.
comment: It is used with SUFI-2 in SWAT calibration; values close to 1 are better.

definition: The sum of the differences between simulated and observed values divided by the sum of observed values, in percent.
comment: It is widely used to evaluate hydrological models; positive values indicate underestimation in the usual hydrological convention.

definition: The difference between a value and a reference value divided by the reference value, in percent.
comment: It is equivalent to the percentage error of a single value.

definition: The difference between a predicted and an observed value divided by the observed value, in percent.
comment: It is used for single values such as annual energy or power density.

definition: The relative difference between the wind power density computed from a fitted distribution and the power density computed from the observed data.
comment: It evaluates how well a wind-speed distribution reproduces the energy content of the wind.

definition: The share of observations that fall within the prediction intervals.
comment: It should be close to the nominal confidence level.

definition: The mean width of the prediction intervals divided by the range of the observations.
comment: Narrower intervals with the same coverage are better.

definition: The average width of the 95 % prediction uncertainty band divided by the standard deviation of the observations.
comment: It is used with SUFI-2 in SWAT calibration; values close to 0 are better.

definition: The sum of the absolute differences between the ranks of alternatives given by two methods.
comment: It compares rankings from different multi-criteria methods.

definition: The bias divided by the mean of the observed values.
comment: It is often given in percent.

definition: The difference between a predicted and an observed value divided by the observed value.
comment: It is often given in percent.

evaluationMetricName: Relative likelihood gain per data point
definition: The gain in log-likelihood of a model over a reference model divided by the number of data points.
comment: It compares the fit of probability models on the same data.

definition: The mean bias error divided by the mean of the observed values.
comment: It is often given in percent.

definition: The root mean square error divided by the mean of the observed values.
comment: It is often expressed in percent; values below 10 % are usually read as excellent.

evaluationMetricName: Right-tail Anderson-Darling statistic of second degree
definition: A variant of the Anderson-Darling statistic that weights the right tail of the distribution.
comment: It is used to assess the fit of distributions to high wind speeds.

definition: The root mean square error divided by the standard deviation of the observed values.
comment: It is used to evaluate hydrological models; lower values are better.

definition: The square root of the mean of the squared differences between predicted and observed values.
comment: It is expressed in the unit of the variable and penalises large errors more than the mean absolute error.

definition: The root mean square error divided by the root mean square error of a naive reference forecast.
comment: Values below 1 indicate that the model beats the naive forecast.

definition: The difference between the skewness and kurtosis of a fitted distribution and those of the data.
comment: It checks whether a fitted distribution reproduces the shape of the empirical distribution.

definition: The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of an estimate.
comment: It measures the precision of an estimated parameter or mean.

definition: A statistic that tests whether the mean difference between predicted and observed values differs significantly from zero.
comment: In the solar radiation literature it is computed from the MBE and the RMSE.

definition: The relative difference between simulated and observed total volumes over a period.
comment: It is used to evaluate the water balance of hydrological models.

definition: The mean absolute error in which each error is multiplied by a weight.
comment: Weights often reflect the frequency or importance of each class or period.
